# PRD: Team Workspaces (v1)

**Author:** [name] | **Status:** Draft for kickoff | **Date:** 2026-10-06

## 1. Overview and Problem

Teams using the app have no shared workspace. Members of the same company cannot collect, manage or access notes in one team-owned space.

**v1 goal:** let a team create a workspace, invite members by email, and share notes inside it.

## 2. Evidence (gaps)

No evidence is available at kickoff. Nothing in this document relies on data, quotes or research.

- GAP: no data on how many accounts currently share notes.
- GAP: no data on how many paid accounts have more than one user.
- GAP: no customer research or quotes on team collaboration needs.
- GAP: no data on typical team size or workspaces needed per account.
- GAP: no competitive or market comparison.

## 3. Goals and Success Metrics

**Primary metric:** 20% of paid accounts create a workspace within 60 days.

Open items for the team to confirm:
- **OPEN:** definition of "paid account" (for example, which plans and statuses count).
- **OPEN:** start of the 60-day window (for example, feature launch or account creation).

**Other metrics:** none defined. Any added later must be labeled "proposed".

## 4. Users and Roles

Two roles only: **Admin** and **Member**.

| Capability | Admin | Member |
|---|---|---|
| Create a workspace | Yes (creator becomes admin; Assumption) | n/a |
| Invite members by email | Yes | Proposed: no |
| Create notes in the workspace | Yes | Yes |
| View and edit shared notes | Proposed: all | Proposed: all |
| Delete shared notes | Proposed: all | Proposed: own notes only |
| Remove members | Proposed: yes | No |
| Change member roles | Proposed: yes | No |
| Delete the workspace | Proposed: yes | No |

Only the existence of the two roles was specified. Every permission above is **proposed** except as noted. Assumption: a workspace has at least one admin at all times.

## 5. Scope

**In (v1)**
- Creating a workspace
- Inviting members by email
- Shared notes within a workspace

**Out (v1)**
- Billing changes
- SSO
- Guest access

**Undecided:** cross-workspace sharing is neither in nor out (see Open Questions).

## 6. Requirements

All requirement details below are Assumptions unless stated otherwise, to be confirmed at kickoff.

**A. Workspace creation**
1. A user can create a workspace with a name. (Assumption: name is the only required field.)
2. The creator becomes the first admin. (Assumption)
3. A workspace has a single, defined member list with roles. (Assumption)
4. Assumption: whether a user can belong to or create multiple workspaces is not specified; see Open Questions.

**B. Inviting members by email**
5. An admin can invite a person by email address. Proposed: members cannot invite.
6. The invitee is assigned a role (admin or member) at invite. (Assumption)
7. The invitee receives an email with a link to join. (Assumption)
8. An admin can see pending invites and revoke them. (Assumption)
9. Assumption: invite expiry and the handling of invitees without an existing account are not specified; see Open Questions.

**C. Shared notes within a workspace**
10. A member can create a note inside a workspace, visible to all workspace members. (Assumption: visibility is workspace-wide by default.)
11. Workspace members can view notes in the workspace; edit and delete rights follow the proposed permissions in section 4.
12. Non-members cannot view or access workspace notes. (Assumption)
13. When a member is removed, they lose access to the workspace's notes. (Assumption)

## 7. Open Questions

1. **Migration of existing shared notes into workspaces.** Left open; no answer proposed or assumed.
   Blocks decisions on:
   - the data model for note ownership and workspace association
   - whether v1 includes any migration tooling or UX
   - the engineering estimate and sequencing
   - design of any migration or onboarding flow
   - launch communication to existing users who share notes
2. **Cross-workspace sharing:** undecided (neither in nor out). Blocks decisions on: note permission model, workspace data isolation, and whether a note can exist in more than one workspace.
3. Definition of "paid account" (blocks metric instrumentation and baseline).
4. Start of the 60-day window (blocks metric instrumentation and reporting).
5. Final permission matrix: confirm or change each "proposed" item in section 4.
6. Can a user belong to or create more than one workspace?
7. Invite handling: expiry, and invitees without an existing account.
8. Who within an account may create a workspace (any user, or only certain users)?

## 8. Risks and Dependencies

**Risks**
- Scope risk: the unresolved migration and cross-workspace questions could change the data model after design and engineering start. (Assumption)
- Permission risk: all permission details are proposed and unvalidated. (Assumption)
- Metric risk: the primary metric cannot be measured until its two definitions are confirmed.
- Evidence risk: with no baseline data, the 20% target cannot be assessed for realism at kickoff.

**Dependencies**
- Email delivery capability for invites. (Assumption)
- Decisions on Open Questions 1 and 2 before the data model is finalized. (Assumption)

## 9. Next Steps for Kickoff

1. Engineering and design leads challenge scope, roles and requirements; record changes.
2. Confirm or amend each "proposed" permission.
3. Assign an owner and a decision date for each Open Question, with Questions 1 and 2 first.
4. Confirm the two metric definitions (paid account, 60-day start).
5. Decide whether design and engineering can start on the in-scope capabilities that do not depend on open questions, and which cannot.
6. Assign owners to close the Evidence gaps.
